exact_question.question: If Charismatic must Recruit but only one Eyrie warrior remains in supply, can placing that one fulfill the Decree?

exact_answer_key.expected_answer: No. Charismatic requires two; inability fully complete causes immediate turmoil despite maximum-possible piece placement.

exact_summary_excerpts.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

**Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** Each card requires:

| Decree column | Match the card's suit to | Required procedure for one card |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |
| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |
| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there** |

**Bird Decree cards are wild in every column:** choose any clearing suit, while still meeting that action’s other requirements.

If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

- **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)

authoritative_source_passages.quotation:
1.1.1     Precedence. If a card conflicts with the Law, fol­
low the card. If the Learning to Play guide con­
flicts with the Law, follow the Law. If you can fol­
low both a general rule and a faction or hireling
rule, follow both; if you cannot, follow the faction
or hireling rule.

1.1.2     Use of Cannot. The term cannot is absolute. It
cannot be overridden unless explicitly instructed.

1.5.1     Limits. Pieces are limited by the contents of the
game. Do not use proxy pieces if you run out.

1.5.4     Piece Manipulation. Pieces are placed and re­
moved as defined in the Glossary (G.20, G.24). If
you are prompted to place, take, or remove pieces
but you cannot do so fully, you must place, take, or
remove the maximum number possible. (This does
not let you avoid costs or prerequisites. You just cannot
do less than the most you can.) If multiple pieces  are

removed simultaneously and that would trigger
effects, remove all pieces before triggering effects.

7.5.2     Resolve the Decree. You must resolve the Decree,
starting with the leftmost column and moving
right. In each column, you must resolve all of its
cards, but in any order. For each card, you must
take the action listed for its column, as follows. If
you cannot fully take an action, you immediately
fall into turmoil (7.7).

I     Recruit. Place a warrior in any clearing with a
roost whose suit matches the card suit.
II     Move. Move from any clearing whose suit
matches the card suit. (You must move at least
one warrior.)
III     Battle. Initiate a battle in any clearing whose
suit matches the card suit.
IV     Build. Place a roost in any clearing you rule
whose suit matches the card suit and which has
no roost.

7.7 Turmoil
If you cannot fully take an action in the Decree (7.5.2)
for any reason, you fall into turmoil. You must take the
Turmoil action as follows in order.
7.7.4     Step 4: Rest. End Daylight and begin Evening.

7.8.2     Charismatic. Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and
Battle. Whenever you take a Recruit action, you
must place two warriors instead of one.

G.20     Place. Take the prompted piece from the prompt­
ed source and put it in the prompted destination.
Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take
it from its supply, or take the leftmost prompted
piece if it is on a track. Put is shorthand for Place.

G.24     Remove. Take the prompted piece from the
prompted source and return it to the prompted
destination. Usually, no destination is specified—
in this case, return it to its owner’s supply, return
it to the rightmost empty space of its track it has
one, or remove it permanently otherwise. (Items
are removed permanently.)

4.2 Move
When you move, take any number (more than zero) of
your warriors and pawns from one clearing and move
them on a linking path (2.2) to one adjacent clearing.
4.2.1     You Must Rule. To take a move, you must rule
the origin clearing, destination clearing, or both.

4.3 Battle
When you battle, choose a clearing with any number
of your warriors and pawns as the clearing of battle.
You are the attacker. Choose an enemy in the clearing
of battle to be the defender.

2.2.3     Slots. Each clearing has a number of building
slots (white boxes). Whenever you place a build­
ing, it fills an open slot. You cannot place a build­
ing in a clearing with no open slots.

2.1.1     Birds Are Wild. You can treat any bird card as a
card of another suit, even if you must spend, take,
or give multiple cards of the same suit. Lb

7.5 Daylight
Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.
7.5.1     Craft. You may activate roosts to craft cards from
your hand.

7.2.1     Crafting. The Eyrie craft before resolving the De­
cree during Daylight by activating roosts.

pdf_inspection.confirmed: 1.1.1, 1.5.4, 7.5.2, 7.5.2.I-IV, 7.7, and 7.8.2 occur in the indicated printed pages; the multi-column text extraction displaces Recruit/Move/Battle/Build in root-rules.txt, but the PDF places them at the top left of page 7 as the continuation of 7.5.2 on page 6. The operative words and paragraph ownership are clear.
pdf_inspection.reason: No disputed symbol or glyph determines this question; direct layout extraction resolves the relevant paragraph order.

interpretation.correct_result: No. The Charismatic Decree Recruit requires two warriors. With only one in supply, the Eyrie cannot fully take that action and immediately enters Turmoil without performing the partial Recruit; the remaining warrior stays in supply.
interpretation.timing: The trigger in 7.5.2 is inability to fully take the action, not a later failed placement attempt or an end-of-action completion check. With a known one-warrior supply and an obligation to place two, that trigger is already satisfied when resolving this card. The instruction is to enter Turmoil immediately. It does not instruct the Eyrie to first attempt or partly resolve the unavailable Recruit.
interpretation.general_rule_analysis: 1.5.4 establishes a real general maximum-possible rule, but its antecedent concerns a prompted piece manipulation. It does not say that an otherwise unavailable action must first be attempted, nor that maximum placement postpones an explicit immediate faction consequence. The cardinality reduction cannot turn the incomplete Recruit into a full Charismatic action; the readers themselves correctly recognize this.
interpretation.hierarchy: 1.1.1 first requires following general and faction rules together if possible, then gives the faction rule priority if they conflict. Applying 1.5.4 to place one before Turmoil conflicts with the Eyrie-specific immediate Turmoil instruction in 7.5.2. The compatible application is to retain the general rule for available piece-manipulation prompts while obeying immediate Turmoil here; it does not generate an intervening partial Recruit.
interpretation.alternative_considered: The competing reading would execute the maximum possible placement and then enter Turmoil because the action remains incomplete. This preserves maximum placement but treats immediate as after an unprovided attempt/completion check. The Eyrie text instead conditions immediate Turmoil directly on inability to fully take the action, which is already known. The faction-priority rule resolves the resulting timing conflict.
interpretation.answer_key_treatment: The key correctly requires No, two warriors, and immediate Turmoil. Its phrase "despite maximum-possible piece placement" is ambiguous about actual placement timing. It is not an authoritative exception permitting a one-warrior partial Recruit; if intended to direct that placement, that portion would conflict with 7.5.2 and 1.1.1. The response is graded against the Law rather than mechanically inheriting that possible key implication.

fact_checklist.fact: Pieces are finite; proxies are forbidden; ordinary placement uses supply or leftmost track space; removal uses supply/rightmost empty track space; items are removed permanently.
Simultaneously removed pieces are all removed before removal-triggered effects.
The quoted Decree procedures require Recruit, Move, Battle, Build in column order, with card order free within each column; bird cards are wild.

The quoted Move requires at least one warrior from a matching-suit origin with ordinary movement requirements; Battle requires a matching-suit clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build requires a matching-suit ruled clearing, an open slot, and no existing roost.
Place the sole available warrior as the maximum possible, then enter Turmoil (or permit that placement in this situation).
fact_checklist.reason: Known inability to take the full two-warrior action triggers Turmoil immediately under the Eyrie-specific rule. A one-warrior Recruit before that trigger postpones the required immediate consequence. Under 1.1.1 the faction rule prevails over incompatible general maximum-placement application.

reader-a.grading_rationale: All literal requested content is supplied correctly across the complete Q41 response: No, two are required, and the shortage leads to immediate Turmoil. No repeated wording in separate fields is demanded. The additional concrete permission/instruction to place one warrior changes board state incorrectly, so the complete response is partial rather than correct. It is not wholly incorrect because its direct answer and central shortage consequence are correct.
reader-a.summary_faithfulness: The quotations are faithful to the supplied summary; that does not independently validate the application against the authoritative Law.
reader-a.wording_note: Although the text says one warrior "may be placed", it first directs "Place the maximum possible". Taken together this asserts permission to perform the one-warrior placement. That material permission is the error; no separate penalty is imposed for may/must wording.
